The DeviceStore interface (oauth/device.go:124-137) has no consume/delete/claim method, and MemoryDeviceStore never deletes, so an approved device_code mints a fresh access+refresh pair on every poll for the whole TTL. RevokeGrant (oauth/grants.go:128-137) only calls tokens.DeleteBySubjectClient, which cannot reach the separate DeviceStore, so a poll after revocation does re-mint with a 30d refresh token; the OP store fix (internal/store/memory/oidc.go:1086-1103) confirms the defect is real, and oauth/zz_probe_test.go (build tag audit5) is a probe that prints exactly this repeat mint. Downgraded from high because it is not reachable in any shipped artifact: the only live device surface is internal/oidchttp (mounted by cmd/re0auth at cmd/re0auth/main.go:575, apiConfig.OIDC = oidcHandler), which consumes an approved device_code on first read and only the OP store is wired. The oauth.Service device endpoints have no HTTP mounter anywhere in the repo: upstreamkit.Server.Handler (upstreamkit/server.go:142-153) mounts authorize/token/revoke/cascade_revocation only and its handleToken rejects the device grant type, and github.com/Re0Auth/r0semi/internal/wiring.OAuthComponent is referenced only by its own tests. Exploiting this requires an embedder to write its own device_authorization + token HTTP wrappers on top of oauth.Service, so severity is conditional; if such an embedder exists the finding should be raised back to high.

verified.reason: Confirmed as written. freeUserCode (oauth/device.go:432-443) only treats errors.Is(err, ErrDeviceNotFound) as 'free'; every other error (persistent-store failure, context cancellation) increments the attempt counter, so after 8 tries it returns the generic errors.New('oauth: could not allocate a unique user code') with the underlying cause dropped and no errors.Is chain. The uniqueness check is also read-then-write: MemoryDeviceStore.SaveDevice (oauth/device.go:155-163) blindly overwrites byUser[NormalizeUserCode(...)], so two concurrent BeginDeviceAuthorization calls could in principle claim the same user code; postgres SaveDevice (internal/store/postgres/oauth.go:603-611) relies on the unique expression index to reject a duplicate. Impact is a misleading 500 / masked infrastructure error plus a theoretical (21^8-space) collision, not an authorization bypass, so low is correct.

Confirmed. The throttle check (oauth/device.go:292-294) runs before the rec.Status switch (302-307), so a decided record polled again inside the interval returns slow_down rather than access_denied/tokens; only a poll outside the interval reaches the terminal answer. The advertised interval is floored: interval := int64(s.pollInterval / time.Second) with a minimum of 1 (lines 252-255), while the throttle compares against the untruncated s.pollInterval (line 292), so a non-integral DevicePollInterval (e.g. 1500ms) advertises 1s but enforces 1.5s and elicits spurious slow_down from a client pacing to the advertised value. Both are correctness/interop nits with defaults (5s) unaffected, no security impact, and RFC 8628's interval is a floor the client must respect, so slow_down before a terminal status merely delays the answer by one interval. Low is appropriate.

Confirmed. handleGetAuthorizationRequest maps every DescribeAuthorization error to 404 not_found 'authorization request expired' (internal/httpapi/authorization_routes.go:97-101), the deny branch maps every DenyAuthorization error to the same 404 (151-155), and writeDecisionError's default case does so for every error that is not *oauth.Error (173-183). A store outage, context deadline or serialization failure is therefore reported to the browser as an expired request with no 5xx and no distinction from the genuinely expired case; the approve path only special-cases *oauth.Error codes access_denied and other protocol errors. This is a real observability/reliability defect. Note the sibling device path does classify unknown/expired vs internal (internal/httpapi/device_routes.go:24-45), which shows the intended shape; low because it masks an outage rather than causing one or granting anything.

Confirmed as a factual code observation. Registry (oauth/scope.go:158-160) has no mutex; Register writes r.byScope[d.Scope] (192-195) while Get (200-203), Descriptors (206-213) and Resolve (217-235) read the same map, so a Register concurrent with a serving request is an unsynchronized read/write on a Go map (fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' or a torn read). The doc comment at 183-184 only states the composition-time convention. No in-repo caller violates it: NewRegistry/DefaultRegistry populate the map before the service is built (oauth/as.go:77), and the only Register calls outside scope.go are tests (oauth/as_test.go:44, oauth/scope_test.go:39-45); OAuthComponent is likewise only used from internal/wiring/oauth_test.go. So the exploit requires an embedding that registers scopes after the server starts, contrary to the documented contract. Low, with the precondition stated rather than assumed; a lazy provider-registration or config-reload embedding would make it a process-killing data race.

verified.reason: Confirmed. describeScopes (oauth/device.go:415-430) calls Registry.Resolve with whatever slice it is given, and Resolve(nil, ...) (oauth/scope.go:217-235) returns an empty descriptor list and nil error, so BeginDeviceAuthorization (224-228) succeeds with zero scopes; the request is stored with Scopes=nil (239-244). DecideDeviceAuthorization then treats scopes==nil as 'grant the requested set' (granted := rec.Scopes at 373, no approval branch entered) and records DeviceApproved, and the poll's fall-through at line 308 calls s.issue with an empty scope slice, minting a scope-less access token plus a 30d refresh token bound to the subject. The impact is bounded: Refresh cannot widen (oauth/as.go:299-307) and every data read checks hasScope, so the credential grants nothing. The shipped OP device path refuses an empty scope outright (internal/oidchttp/oidchttp.go:1157-1162, plus the authorize path at 1065-1069), and again neither device endpoint is mounted for oauth.Service in any shipped binary, so this is a library contract defect rather than a live exposure. Low is appropriate.

summary: Verified 9/9 findings against the cited sources plus callers, mounts and stores the discovery auditor may have under-weighted. 5 confirmed at low (S04-5 misleading user-code allocation error and non-atomic uniqueness, S04-6 slow_down-before-terminal plus floored advertised interval, S04-7 consent-store failures reported as 'authorization request expired', S04-8 unsynchronized Registry.Register, S04-9 scope-less device authorization and token pair); 0 rejected; 4 downgraded. S04-1 was downgraded high->medium: the unconditional re-issue and revocation bypass are real and the OP store's own fix confirms the defect, but oauth.Service's device endpoints are not mounted by any shipped binary or HTTP wrapper (cmd/re0auth serves the consuming OP path; upstreamkit mounts no device grant; OAuthComponent is test-only), so exploitation requires a custom embedding - if such an embedder exists it is high. S04-2 (medium->low), S04-3 (medium->low) and S04-4 (medium->low) share the same reachability defect: the confidential-client check, the non-expiring MemoryDeviceStore and the full-scan MemoryStore are all properties of the unmounted/dev-test oauth.Service/MemoryStore, while the live OP path already authenticates device clients, consumes approved codes, refuses empty scopes and indexes device records by user code and grants by subject. No new severe finding was identified; the tests cited (oauth/zz_probe_test.go) are build-tagged probes and were treated as corroboration, not as a source of the claims.
